messages:
Sam: Heads-up — getting a customer escalation: multiple 502/504 from hosted inference endpoint since 03:20 UTC. Customer reports >30s timeouts and repeated retries. I see a burst of requests and then gateway 504s. Investigating autoscale path.

Priya: Customer: 'our product started timing out at scale — intermittent 5xxs, only started after yesterday's traffic spike'. They included request ids and timestamps.

Alyssa: Thanks. Which cluster/namespace? Any recent deploys? :eyes:

Sam: Namespace: redwood-hosted-prod, model-route: /v1/generate/llama-13b. No deploys in the window per deploy-bot (see below).

deploy-bot: deploy check — no service rollouts in the last 6h for redwood-hosted-prod.

Miguel: Pasted logs from runtime on one failing pod: 
```
2026-03-15T03:20:12Z runtime INFO serve request id=abc123 start
2026-03-15T03:20:30Z runtime WARN model-init duration=22.4s model=llama-13b kvcache-load=18.9s
2026-03-15T03:20:33Z kubelet WARN Readiness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 502
2026-03-15T03:20:33Z runtime ERROR request id=abc123 failed: upstream timeout
```
Looks like model initialization + KV-cache restore is taking ~20s and readiness probe is failing which prevents the pod from joining the endpoint quickly.

Priya: So pods are stuck in NotReady, K8s/HPA/KEDA don't count them for service capacity and the gateway hits 0 backends => 5xx/gateway. Customer sees retries and timeouts.

Alyssa: Do we see KEDA ScaledObject events? KEDA polling intervals can delay scale up if activation is missed.

Miguel: Yup — here's the ScaledObject for the route (sensitive fields removed):
```
apiVersion: keda.sh/v1alpha1
kind: ScaledObject
metadata:
  name: so-llama-13b
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    name: runtime-deployment-llama-13b
  pollingInterval: 30     # default
  cooldownPeriod: 300     # big cooldown
  minReplicaCount: 0
  triggers:
  - type: external
    metadata:
      url: https://metrics.internal/api/queue/llama-13b
      threshold: "10"
```
If traffic is bursty and minReplicaCount==0, we rely on KEDA polls/activation; poll=30s + model init ~20s => not fast enough. Also cooldownPeriod 300s can prevent quick re-scale if oscillation suspected.

Nora: Customer asks: why are we scale-to-zeroing models that take >15s to warm? They want a recommendation (or dedicated capacity).

Sam: Short-term mitigation: increase minReplicaCount to 1 or set minReplicaCount 2 for critical routes. Medium-term: reduce pollingInterval to 5s and set activationThreshold lower, or use KEDA trigger that watches queue length via push rather than poll. Also add startupProbe to the pod so K8s won't kill container during initialization.

Miguel: Repro steps I ran locally to recreate 504s:
1) Scale down runtime-deployment-llama-13b to 0 replicas.
2) Fire 50 concurrent requests at the endpoint over 10s using hey: `hey -n 200 -c 50 https://hosted.redwood.ai/v1/generate/llama-13b`
3) Observe KEDA ScaledObject reacting ~30s later, pods arriving but readiness probes failing, gateway returns 502/504 during warmup.

Alyssa: Can we patch a quick fix to reduce customer pain? Suggestion: patch ScaledObject pollingInterval=5 and minReplicaCount=1 for the route, and bump readinessProbe initialDelaySeconds to 30 or add a startupProbe.

Miguel: I can push a temporary k8s patch to the staging cluster to validate. But for prod I want an owner approval. Changing minReplicaCount has cost implications — tradeoff with customer uptime.

Priya: I'll coordinate with the customer: propose two options: 1) temporary increase minReplicaCount to 1 (we absorb cost for 24-72h) to stop 5xxs; 2) recommend Dedicated capacity if predictable high QPS. Which shall I offer?

Sam: Let's offer option 1 immediate, option 2 for long-term. Miguel — can you prepare a short PR with the ScaledObject patch + readiness/startupProbe change? Alyssa — please approve emergency patch timeline.

Miguel: Will do. Plan:
- Patch 1: set minReplicaCount=1 for so-llama-13b and pollingInterval=5 for 1h, monitor.
- Patch 2: add startupProbe to runtime container: `startupProbe.httpGet.path=/healthy?startup=true initialDelaySeconds=5 periodSeconds=5 failureThreshold=30` so kubelet waits up to ~150s for model init.
- If symptoms persist, set minReplicaCount=2 and escalate to Product for Dedicated upsell.

Alyssa: Approved for emergency patch. Post the exact kubectl patch here before applying. Also add a Grafana dashboard panel to watch readyReplicas and KEDA scaledobject activations.

Miguel: Kubectl patch I'm going to run (dry-run):
```
kubectl patch scaledobject so-llama-13b --type='merge' -p '{"spec":{"minReplicaCount":1,"pollingInterval":5}}' -n redwood-hosted-prod --dry-run=client -o yaml
```
And the container patch (startupProbe):
```
kubectl patch deployment runtime-deployment-llama-13b -n redwood-hosted-prod --patch 'spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: runtime
        startupProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthy?startup=true
            port: 8080
          periodSeconds: 5
          failureThreshold: 30'
```
I'll apply after approvals.

Priya: I'll reply to customer now: "we're investigating an autoscale warmup issue. Short-term we can disable scale-to-zero for your critical route to prevent warmup 5xxs; we'll monitor and follow up with a permanent tuning or Dedicated option."

Nora: Customer accepted the short-term option, wants timeline and rollback plan.

Sam: Add rollback: revert minReplicaCount to 0 and pollingInterval back to 30 after monitoring window if traffic stabilizes. Also add note to runbook: model-init longer than 15s => set minReplicaCount>0 or prewarm.

Alyssa: I'll create an incident runbook ticket with steps to patch, monitor, and rollback and assign to Miguel. Also add an alert burn rate/GW-5xx spike runbook.

Miguel: Applying patch now to prod (will report back).

keda-bot: ScaledObject so-llama-13b updated: minReplicaCount=1 pollingInterval=5 (applied by Miguel).

Miguel: Patch applied. Observability: readyReplicas from 0 -> 1 within 18s, gateway 5xx rate dropped to near-zero. Will keep monitoring for 30m.

Sam: Great. After 30m and green, we document root cause as: scale-to-zero + KEDA default poll + long model init => readiness failures -> no backends -> gateway 5xx. Action items: docs/runbook update (Sam), runtime startupProbe defaults (Miguel), sales/CS note about Dedicated for low-latency guarantees (Nora/Priya).

Priya: Customer notified, they appreciate quick triage. Marking incident as 'mitigated' pending 24h observation. :thumbsup:
